text:
Anthropic released the Claude 4 family in May 2025 as two distinct models—Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4—to address different performance tiers within its product lineup [Source: ev-1]. The flagship model, Opus 4, was positioned for maximum capability, while Sonnet 4 served as a "fast workhorse" designed to be the developer-default coding model at a lower price point of $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, compared to Opus 4's pricing of $15 and $75 respectively [Source: ev-1].

The launch signaled that agentic coding had become a defining market segment in 2025, driven by products like Claude Code [Source: ev-1]. By introducing "computer use 2.0," which offered browser control roughly twice as reliable as the previous generation, Anthropic positioned itself against competitors such as OpenAI’s o-series during an enterprise gold rush for agentic tools [Source: ev-1]. The release emphasized reliability and safety, aiming to establish Claude 4 as the most dependable coding agent, a strategy that contributed to record API usage and helped cement Anthropic's position as a leader in the coding-agent space [Source: ev-1].
